program.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
program.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

requirements.text: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
requirements.source_phrase: Move the mug to the right of the headphones

outcomes.description: Move the mug so that it is positioned to the right of the headphones.
outcomes.target: The mug is visibly positioned to the right of the headphones.
outcomes.reference: The headphones in the image; compare the mug’s position with the headphones.

nodes.question: Does the edited image reliably show that the source blue mug itself was moved to the right of the headphones, rather than remaining at its former position while a different mug is on the right?
nodes.criteria: Compare the source blue mug, including its distinctive body and handle, with objects in the edited image and assess its position relative to the same headphones. Pass only when visual evidence reliably supports that the source mug itself is now to the right of the headphones. Fail only when evidence reliably establishes that the source mug was not moved there. Use unknown when blur, appearance changes, or other ambiguity prevents reliable determination of the source mug's identity or movement. A mug appearing on the right alone does not establish that the source mug was moved.
nodes.binding: Cross-image binding: the blue mug in the source image and the same headphones in the source and edited images; compare the source mug with the edited mugs and assess the source mug's position relative to the headphones in the edited image, allowing for changes in scale, lighting, and appearance.

nodes.question: In the edited image, is a mug visibly positioned to the right of the headphones?
nodes.criteria: Inspect the edited image and compare the visible mug or mugs with the headphones. Pass only if a mug is clearly positioned to the right of the headphones. Fail if the image reliably shows no mug to their right. Use unknown if the objects or their relative positions cannot be determined reliably. This checks only the final spatial relation for a mug in the edited image; it does not establish that the source mug itself was moved.
nodes.binding: Edited image only: the visible mug or mugs and the headphones; assess their left-to-right positions.

program.checker_template: Evaluate ONE independent required condition against the SOURCE and EDITED images. No reference label, previous answers or optimization feedback is supplied. Return pass if the condition is satisfied, fail if it is not satisfied, or unknown if the evidence cannot establish an answer. Inspect only this saved condition, its criteria and binding. Report factual evidence and confidence (0..1 or null). A pass means satisfaction of THIS condition, not an overall edit label. Do not anticipate the optimizer's target. Missing evidence or transport/schema failures must not become a negative observation. The final overall label is computed by code; you never supply it.

d2: The current binding and criterion test only whether any mug is right of the headphones, so the trace passes on the rightmost mug even though the edited image also shows a mug left of the headphones and a blurred blue remnant where the original mug was. That establishes some progress, not complete fulfillment; the aggregate/reference mismatch likely reflects that this single binary check cannot distinguish partial from complete. For typed structural edits, preserve the final-image spatial check but make its scope and output semantics explicit: assess all visible mugs and their positions, and distinguish a clearly supported partial result from complete fulfillment only when the node has evidence relevant to the requested move (including source-to-edited comparison). Do not infer that the rightmost mug is the moved source mug from the edited image alone. Keep uncertainty for ambiguous object identity or position; the trace is valid, queried, and has no dependency or transport failure, so this is a criterion/coverage limitation rather than a visual-evidence or execution failure.
d1: The node already correctly binds the source blue mug to the edited image and treats the right-side mug alone as insufficient; the trace is valid and queried, with no transport or dependency failure. The edited image shows a mug on each side of the headphones, but the source mug’s former location is only a blurred blue patch, so its identity and movement remain uncertain. Do not force a partial label from that ambiguity: the reference label is aggregate guidance, not atomic ground truth. The actionable limitation is that this single binary decision cannot express partial progress. In typed structural edits, preserve the identity and spatial checks, but make the node’s output semantics capable of representing supported progress separately from complete fulfillment, and assess all relevant visible mugs and the former position. Keep uncertainty when the source mug cannot be reliably matched; do not treat low confidence or variation as proof that the requested move is absent.

observations.evidence: The edited image shows two small mugs: one to the left of the headphones and one to their right. Neither clearly retains the source mug’s distinctive blue body and left-facing handle; the blue-looking area at the former position is heavily blurred and does not establish the mug’s identity or movement. Thus the right-side mug alone is insufficient to determine whether the source mug was moved there.
In the edited image, a visible mug is on the right side of the headphones, with the mug clearly farther right in the image.

Replace them with one requirement-mapped decision that distinguishes complete fulfillment from supported partial progress, while preserving uncertainty when the source mug cannot be matched reliably. decisions.criteria: Compare the source mug with all visible mugs in the edited image, assess their positions relative to the same headphones, and inspect the source mug’s former location. Pass only if evidence reliably establishes that the source mug itself is now to the right of the headphones. Fail only if evidence reliably establishes that the requested move made no progress. Use unknown if source-mug identity, movement, or relevant positions cannot be determined reliably. A mug on the right alone does not establish that the source mug was moved. If evidence establishes some relevant progress but not that the source mug itself reached the right side, treat that as partial progress rather than complete fulfillment or no progress.
